new_entities.name: Maternal gestational diabetes
new_entities.description: Hyperglycemia meeting gestational diabetes criteria during pregnancy.

new_entities.name: Long-term child obesity
aliases: childhood and adolescent obesity after GDM exposure
new_entities.description: Overweight or obesity risk in childhood through adolescence among offspring exposed to gestational diabetes in utero.

edges.effect_quant: In utero exposure to gestational diabetes is associated with higher obesity risk later in childhood and adolescence, and the risk appears lower when maternal glycemia is tightly controlled.
edges.population: children and adolescents exposed to gestational diabetes in utero
edges.mechanism: Fetal exposure to maternal hyperglycemia can promote higher insulin exposure, altered adiposity programming, and birth-size shifts that track into later obesity risk. The attenuation of risk with better maternal glycemic control supports a biologically meaningful intrauterine component rather than pure family confounding.
edges.summary: The most informative recent evidence shows that gestational diabetes is linked to higher offspring obesity risk well beyond infancy, with persistence into school age and adolescence. Large cohorts also suggest that prompt and sustained glucose control during pregnancy can narrow that excess risk, which makes this edge both predictive and actionable.
edges.caveats: Maternal prepregnancy BMI explains part of the signal and should not be ignored. The safest read is that gestational diabetes adds risk on top of underlying maternal metabolic vulnerability rather than acting as a completely separate pathway in every family.

evidence.citation: MayaJ et al 2025 J Clin Endocrinol Metab
evidence.notes: Gestational Glucose Intolerance and Risk of Obesity in Childhood and Adolescence.
